question: In which year did Babur defeat Ibrahim Lodi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1526.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat (पानीपत का पहला युद्ध) in 1526 CE.

• This victory ended the Lodi dynasty (the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate) and marked the foundation of the Mughal Empire in India.

• Babur used field artillery and the Tulughma (flanking) tactic, which gave him a decisive edge despite a smaller army.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Babur was a descendant of Timur (father's side) and Genghis Khan (mother's side).

• He wrote his memoir, the Baburnama, in Chagatai Turkish.

• He later won the Battle of Khanwa (1527) against Rana Sanga and the Battle of Ghaghra (1529).

NOTE

• 1515 (Option 1): No major battle of Babur in India occurred this year; he had not yet invaded India.

• 1530 (Option 3): The year Babur died and was succeeded by his son Humayun.

• 1535 (Option 4): Falls within Humayun's reign, unrelated to the defeat of Ibrahim Lodi.

question: Who was the first female Jawan in the Indian Army?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shanti Tigga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shanti Tigga (शांति तिग्गा) became the first woman jawan (soldier in the ranks) of the Indian Army when she joined the 969 Railway Engineer Regiment of the Territorial Army in 2011.

• She was from Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal, and enrolled at the age of about 35.

• During training she outperformed many male recruits, excelling in firing and physical tests.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A jawan refers to a soldier in the non-officer ranks, distinct from a commissioned officer.

• Shanti Tigga was honoured as the 'Best Trainee' among 1,300 recruits at her centre.

• She held the rank of Lance Naik in the Territorial Army.

NOTE

• Punita Arora (Option 1): First woman to become Lieutenant General in the Indian Army and first woman Vice Admiral in the Navy — an officer, not a jawan.

• Anjali Gupta (Option 3): An officer in the Indian Air Force, known for a disciplinary controversy — not the first female jawan.

• Navjot Kaur (Option 4): An Indian wrestler, unrelated to the Army.

question: Pankaj Advani received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2006. He is associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Billiards and Snooker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pankaj Advani is a legendary Indian cue-sport player associated with Billiards and Snooker (बिलियर्ड्स और स्नूकर).

• He received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (now Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna) in 2006, India's highest sporting honour.

• He is a multiple-time World Billiards and World Snooker champion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (2009) and the Padma Bhushan (2018).

• He is famous for winning the 'Grand Double' — both time and point formats of world billiards in the same year.

• He has won more than two dozen world titles across billiards and snooker.

NOTE

• Chess (Option 1): India's top chess icon is Viswanathan Anand, not Pankaj Advani.

• Table Tennis (Option 3): A different racket sport; players include Achanta Sharath Kamal.

• Tennis (Option 4): A lawn racket sport; not Advani's discipline.

question: In 2025, Shri Jayant Chaudhary launched _____, a Women Entrepreneurship Programme.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swavalambini.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2025, Union Minister of State Shri Jayant Chaudhary launched 'Swavalambini' (स्वावलंबिनी), a Women Entrepreneurship Programme.

• It was launched by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in partnership with IIE Guwahati for the North Eastern states.

• The aim is to make women students job creators rather than job seekers by nurturing entrepreneurial skills.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The programme was rolled out through Higher Education Institutions in the Northeast (Assam, Meghalaya, Sikkim, etc.).

• MSDE implements it via the Indian Institute of Entrepreneurship (IIE), Guwahati.

• It focuses on entrepreneurship awareness, mentoring and hand-holding of women students.

NOTE

• Mahila Samridhi Yojana (Option 1): A micro-finance scheme under the National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation for women of backward classes.

• Udyogini (Option 2): A scheme supporting women entrepreneurs through subsidised loans, not this 2025 launch.

• Stree Shakti (Option 3): A women's self-help-group/savings package (associated with SBI), not the programme launched here.

question: The National Mission on Natural Farming, which was launched in November 2024 aims to promote chemical-free farming among _____ crores farmers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was launched in November 2024 to promote chemical-free farming (रसायन-मुक्त खेती).

• It aims to reach about 1 crore farmers and cover roughly 7.5 lakh hectares.

• It is a standalone Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The mission has an outlay of around Rs. 2,481 crore (Centre's share about Rs. 1,584 crore).

• It promotes locally produced, livestock-based inputs like Jeevamrit and Beejamrit.

• Around 15,000 Model Natural Farming clusters are planned in Gram Panchayats.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 2): Not the target figure for NMNF's farmer coverage.

• 3 (Option 3): Incorrect; overstates the mission's stated reach.

• 4 (Option 4): Incorrect; not the number of crore farmers targeted.

question: India ranks _____ in the Energy Transition Index 2025.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 71st.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India ranked 71st in the Energy Transition Index (ETI) 2025 (ऊर्जा संक्रमण सूचकांक 2025).

• The index is published by the World Economic Forum (WEF).

• It assesses countries on energy security, sustainability and equity/affordability of their energy systems.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sweden topped the Energy Transition Index 2025.

• India has been among the fastest-improving major economies on energy transition in recent years.

• The index covers over 100 countries worldwide.

NOTE

• 9th (Option 1): Not India's rank; this is far higher than India's actual position.

• 46th (Option 2): Incorrect rank for India in ETI 2025.

• 59th (Option 4): Incorrect; not India's ETI 2025 position.

question: India Meteorological Department officially adopted the Bharat Forecast System on 26 May 2025. It has been developed by _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bharat Forecast System (BFS) was developed by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune (भारतीय उष्णकटिबंधीय मौसम विज्ञान संस्थान).

• The India Meteorological Department (IMD) officially adopted it on 26 May 2025.

• It is the world's highest-resolution weather model of its kind, offering forecasts at about 6 km resolution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• IITM Pune is an autonomous institute under the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).

• The BFS improves prediction of localised heavy rainfall and extreme weather events.

• It uses a Tropical Analysis and Prediction System (TGLM)-based dynamical core suited to the tropics.

NOTE

• IIT Kanpur (Option 1): A premier engineering institute, but not the developer of the BFS.

• IIT Kharagpur (Option 2): Not associated with developing the Bharat Forecast System.

• IIT Bombay (Option 3): Not the developer of this weather forecasting model.

question: Which state topped in the Management effectiveness evaluation of protected areas for 2020-2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kerala (केरल) topped the Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE) of protected areas for 2020-2025.

• The MEE is conducted to assess how effectively national parks and wildlife sanctuaries are managed.

• The framework is guided by the IUCN-WCPA methodology and coordinated in India by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kerala's protected areas include Periyar Tiger Reserve, Silent Valley and Eravikulam National Park.

• MEE evaluates areas across parameters such as planning, inputs, processes, outputs and outcomes.

• The evaluation helps identify management gaps and best practices in conservation.

NOTE

• Sikkim (Option 1): Known for Khangchendzonga National Park, but did not top this MEE cycle.

• Tripura (Option 2): A northeastern state; not the topper of this evaluation.

• Manipur (Option 3): Home to Keibul Lamjao National Park, but not the top-ranked state here.

question: Who wrote the autobiography 'Childhood Days: A Memoir'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satyajit Ray.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The autobiography 'Childhood Days: A Memoir' was written by the legendary filmmaker Satyajit Ray (सत्यजीत रे).

• It is an English translation of his Bengali memoir 'Jakhan Choto Chilam'.

• Ray was a celebrated film director, writer and illustrator from Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Satyajit Ray directed the classic 'Pather Panchali' (1955), part of the Apu Trilogy.

• He received the Bharat Ratna (1992) and an Honorary Academy Award (Oscar) in 1992.

• He created the fictional detective Feluda and the scientist Professor Shonku.

NOTE

• Amartya Sen (Option 2): Nobel laureate economist; wrote 'Home in the World', not this book.

• Soumitra Chatterjee (Option 3): Acclaimed Bengali actor who starred in many Ray films, but not the author.

• Rabindranath Tagore (Option 4): Nobel-laureate poet; wrote 'My Reminiscences', a different memoir.

question: Harappan cities had a _____ grid pattern of layout with roads that cut each other at right angles.
solution_text:
The correct answer is rectangular.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harappan (Indus Valley) cities followed a rectangular grid pattern (आयताकार ग्रिड) of town planning.

• The roads and streets cut each other at right angles, dividing the city into neat blocks.

• This reflects the advanced and systematic urban planning of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Cities like Mohenjo-daro and Harappa had a Citadel (upper town) and a Lower Town.

• They featured an advanced drainage system with covered drains along the streets.

• The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro is a notable example of Harappan engineering.

NOTE

• circular (Option 1): Not the layout of Harappan cities; their roads formed rectangular blocks.

• hexagonal (Option 3): Incorrect; no six-sided grid pattern was used.

• triangular (Option 4): Incorrect; streets crossed at right angles, not in triangles.

question: The dance form known as 'Luddi' is popular in which Indian state/Union Territory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'Luddi' (लुड्डी) is a folk dance form popular in the state of Punjab.

• It is a celebratory dance performed to mark victories or joyous occasions.

• Dancers typically sway their heads and move their hands in a snake-like, rhythmic motion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other famous folk dances of Punjab include Bhangra (male) and Giddha (female).

• Punjabi folk dances are usually performed to the beat of the dhol.

• Such dances are prominent during Baisakhi and harvest celebrations.

NOTE

• Meghalaya (Option 1): Known for dances like Nongkrem and Shad Suk Mynsiem, not Luddi.

• Assam (Option 3): Famous for the Bihu dance, not Luddi.

• Andaman and Nicobar (Option 4): Known for tribal Nicobarese dances, not Luddi.

question:
Which of the following is correct regarding medium earth orbit?
I. Satellites in MEO do not need to follow specific paths around Earth
II. MEO is very commonly used by navigation satellites.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Medium Earth Orbit (MEO / मध्यम पृथ्वी कक्षा) lies between about 2,000 km and 35,786 km altitude.

• Statement I: Satellites in MEO are not restricted to specific fixed paths and can occupy various orbital planes.

• Statement II: MEO is very commonly used by navigation satellites — hence both statements are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Navigation systems such as GPS (USA), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (EU) and BeiDou (China) operate in MEO.

• A typical MEO navigation satellite has an orbital period of about 12 hours.

• MEO lies above Low Earth Orbit (LEO) and below Geostationary Orbit (GEO).

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incomplete, as statement II is also correct.

• Only II (Option 2): Incomplete, as statement I is also correct.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Wrong, since both statements are true.

question: In 2025, IIT-Madras and ISRO jointly developed a semiconductor chip. What is the name of this chip?
solution_text:
The correct answer is IRIS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 2025, IIT Madras and ISRO jointly developed and successfully booted an indigenous semiconductor chip named 'IRIS' (आईरिस).

• It is an Atmanirbhar (self-reliant), aerospace-grade microprocessor built on the indigenous SHAKTI processor design.

• It is aimed at meeting India's space and strategic electronics needs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The SHAKTI processor is an open-source RISC-V based design developed at IIT Madras.

• The chip supports 'Make in India' and reduces dependence on imported space-grade processors.

• It was fabricated using indigenous design and testing capabilities.

NOTE

• PRITHVI (Option 1): The name of an Indian surface-to-surface ballistic missile, not this chip.

• SARYU (Option 3): A river in India; not the name of the developed semiconductor chip.

• VIKRAM (Option 4): Name associated with ISRO's lander (Chandrayaan) and the Vikram processor lineage, but not the answer here.

question: During the free fall of an object, as it falls, what happens to its potential energy and kinetic energy?
option_1: Both potential energy and kinetic energy decrease
option_2: Both potential energy and kinetic energy increase
option_3: Potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases
option_4: Potential energy increases while kinetic energy decreases
solution_text:
The correct answer is Potential energy decreases while kinetic energy increases.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During free fall, as an object falls, its height decreases, so its potential energy (स्थितिज ऊर्जा) decreases.

• Its speed increases, so its kinetic energy (गतिज ऊर्जा) increases.

• This is a direct consequence of the law of conservation of mechanical energy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Total mechanical energy (PE + KE) remains constant in the absence of air resistance.

• Potential energy is given by PE = mgh and kinetic energy by KE = ½mv².

• At the moment just before hitting the ground, KE is maximum and PE is minimum.

NOTE

• Both PE and KE decrease (Option 1): Wrong; KE actually rises as speed increases.

• Both PE and KE increase (Option 2): Wrong; PE falls as height reduces.

• PE increases while KE decreases (Option 4): Opposite of what happens during a fall.

question: As of July 2025, which of the following public sector enterprise is awarded with "Maharatna" status?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Power Finance Corporation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Power Finance Corporation (PFC / पावर फाइनेंस कॉर्पोरेशन) holds Maharatna status among Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs).

• PFC was granted Maharatna status in October 2021.

• Maharatna CPSEs enjoy the greatest financial and operational autonomy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Maharatna category was introduced in 2010 by the Department of Public Enterprises.

• A Maharatna board can invest up to Rs. 5,000 crore in a single project without government approval.

• PFC is a leading NBFC financing the power sector in India.

NOTE

• Bharat Electronics Limited (Option 1): A defence PSU with Navratna status, not Maharatna.

• Engineers India Limited (Option 2): A Navratna engineering consultancy PSU, not Maharatna.

• Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (Option 4): A Navratna railway infrastructure PSU, not Maharatna.

question: The disinvestment of a public sector unit leads to _____.
option_1: reduction in financial assets of the government
option_2: increase in the financial assets of the government
option_3: creation of liability of the government
option_4: increase in the tax revenue of the government
solution_text:
The correct answer is reduction in financial assets of the government.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Disinvestment (विनिवेश) means the government sells its shareholding in a public sector unit.

• Since the government's ownership stake (a financial asset) in the PSU falls, it leads to a reduction in the financial assets of the government.

• In return the government receives cash, but its holding of equity (a financial asset) declines.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Disinvestment is handled by the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) under the Ministry of Finance.

• Types include minority, majority (strategic) disinvestment and complete privatisation.

• It helps in reducing fiscal deficit and improving PSU efficiency.

NOTE

• increase in the financial assets of the government (Option 2): Wrong; assets fall, not rise.

• creation of liability of the government (Option 3): Incorrect; disinvestment does not create a liability.

• increase in the tax revenue of the government (Option 4): Incorrect; sale proceeds are capital receipts, not tax revenue.

question: On the bank of which river was the first English factory established?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hugli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per NCERT, the first English factory in Bengal was set up on the banks of the river Hugli (हुगली) in 1651.

• A 'factory' here meant a trading post/warehouse of the English East India Company, not a manufacturing unit.

• It served as a base for the Company's commercial activities in Bengal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The English East India Company was founded in 1600 under a charter from Queen Elizabeth I.

• The Company later built Fort William at Calcutta on the Hugli.

• The Hugli is a distributary of the Ganga flowing through West Bengal.

NOTE

• Ganga (Option 1): A major river, but the referenced first English factory here was on the Hugli.

• Kaveri (Option 2): A South Indian river; not linked to the first English factory in Bengal.

• Mahanadi (Option 3): Flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha; not the site of this factory.

question: In which year the Nawab of Awadh was forced to give over half of his territory to the East India Company?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1801.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1801, the Nawab of Awadh (अवध के नवाब), Saadat Ali Khan, was forced to cede more than half of his territory to the East India Company.

• This was done through a subsidiary alliance treaty signed with the Company.

• The move was engineered under Lord Wellesley, who was Governor-General at the time.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Subsidiary Alliance system was devised by Lord Wellesley.

• Under it, the Indian ruler had to maintain a British force and cede territory or pay for it.

• Awadh was finally annexed by Lord Dalhousie in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance.

NOTE

• 1795 (Option 1): Precedes the subsidiary alliance treaty with Awadh.

• 1810 (Option 3): Not the year of this territorial cession.

• 1818 (Option 4): Associated with the end of the Third Anglo-Maratha War, not the Awadh cession.

question: The Banking Codes and Standards of India (BCSBI) has released a "Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers" (Code) in July _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2006.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (BCSBI) released the "Code of Bank's Commitment to Customers" (ग्राहकों के प्रति बैंक की प्रतिबद्धता संहिता) in July 2006.

• The Code sets minimum standards of banking practice for member banks to follow while dealing with customers.

• It aims to promote fair banking practices, transparency and customer protection.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• BCSBI was set up in 2006 on the recommendation of the S.S. Tarapore Committee.

• It was an independent, autonomous body registered as a society.

• The RBI later merged BCSBI's functions; it ceased independent operations around 2021.

NOTE

• 2004 (Option 1): BCSBI had not yet been established; the Code was not released this year.

• 2008 (Option 3): Later than the actual release year of the first Code.

• 2002 (Option 4): Too early; predates the formation of BCSBI.

question: In which of the following state of India more than 85% of its net sown area is under irrigation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Haryana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Haryana (हरियाणा), more than 85% of the net sown area is under irrigation (सिंचाई).

• This is due to an extensive canal network and widespread use of tube wells.

• Along with Punjab, Haryana is among the most intensively irrigated states in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Haryana is a key contributor to the Green Revolution and to the central foodgrain pool.

• Major crops include wheat, rice, bajra and sugarcane.

• The Western Yamuna Canal and Bhakra canal system are important irrigation sources.

NOTE

• Bihar (Option 1): Has substantial irrigation but not more than 85% of its net sown area.

• Odisha (Option 2): Largely rain-fed agriculture with lower irrigation coverage.

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): A large agricultural state, but its irrigated share is well below 85%.

question: What is the total length (in km) of navigable waterways in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14500.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has about 14,500 km of navigable waterways (नौकायन योग्य जलमार्ग).

• These include rivers, canals, backwaters and creeks.

• Inland water transport is a cheap and eco-friendly mode of transport.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) was set up in 1986 to develop and regulate them.

• National Waterway-1 (Ganga, Haldia to Prayagraj) is one of the major waterways.

• India has declared over 100 National Waterways.

NOTE

• 6500 (Option 1): Understates the total length of India's navigable waterways.

• 8000 (Option 2): Incorrect; less than the standard figure of about 14,500 km.

• 11200 (Option 3): Incorrect; still short of the total navigable length.

question: As per India's Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011, the total households in the country (Rural plus Urban) was _____ crores.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 24.49.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 (सामाजिक आर्थिक एवं जाति जनगणना 2011), the total households (Rural + Urban) were about 24.49 crore.

• The SECC 2011 was the first caste-based census since 1931.

• It captured socio-economic status of households across India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• SECC 2011 was conducted by the Ministry of Rural Development (rural) and Ministry of Housing & Urban Poverty Alleviation (urban).

• Its data is used to identify beneficiaries of welfare schemes like PMAY and Ayushman Bharat.

• It recorded data on deprivation, occupation and income of households.

NOTE

• 27.97 (Option 2): Not the total-households figure reported by SECC 2011.

• 11.97 (Option 3): Incorrect; far below the actual number of households.

• 31.28 (Option 4): Overstates the total households recorded in SECC 2011.

question: How many total districts were covered in the India's Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 survey?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 640.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011 survey covered 640 districts of India.

• This matches the number of districts recorded in the Census of India 2011.

• The exercise gathered detailed household-level socio-economic data.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• SECC 2011 covered around 24.49 crore households across the country.

• It was carried out in both rural and urban areas.

• The data forms the basis for targeting government welfare schemes.

• 680 (Option 2): Incorrect; more than the 640 districts of the 2011 Census.

• 750 (Option 3): Incorrect; overstates the number of districts covered.

• 730 (Option 4): Incorrect; not the number of districts in the SECC 2011 survey.

question: How does auxin affect the growth of the plant in response to light?
option_1: It causes all cells to grow equally
option_2: It stimulates cells on the light side to grow longer
option_3: It inhibits growth on the shady side
option_4: It stimulates cells on the shady side to grow longer
solution_text:
The correct answer is It stimulates cells on the shady side to grow longer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Auxin (ऑक्सिन) is a plant hormone that regulates growth in response to light (phototropism).

• When light falls on one side, auxin moves to the shady (darker) side, where it stimulates cells to elongate.

• As the shady-side cells grow longer, the shoot bends toward the light.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Auxin was the first plant hormone to be discovered.

• It also controls apical dominance, root initiation and cell elongation.

• Positive phototropism of shoots helps plants maximise photosynthesis.

NOTE

• It causes all cells to grow equally (Option 1): Wrong; growth is unequal, causing bending.

• It stimulates cells on the light side to grow longer (Option 2): Wrong; auxin concentrates on the shady side, not the lit side.

• It inhibits growth on the shady side (Option 3): Opposite of reality; the shady side grows more.

question: Which of the following varnas in Vedic society was considered responsible for trade and business?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vaishya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Vedic society, the Vaishya (वैश्य) varna was considered responsible for trade, business and agriculture.

• The Vedic society was divided into four varnas: Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra.

• Vaishyas engaged in commerce, cattle-rearing and cultivation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The concept of four varnas is mentioned in the Purusha Sukta of the Rigveda.

• The varna system was originally based on occupation in early Vedic times.

• Over time it became more rigid and hereditary.

NOTE

• Brahmin (Option 2): The priestly and teaching class, responsible for religious and scholarly duties.

• Shudra (Option 3): The serving class, tasked with serving the other three varnas.

• Kshatriya (Option 4): The warrior and ruling class, responsible for governance and protection.
